questions.q: What is the most common format for BI Publisher financial report templates, and how is it built?
options: A proprietary binary format requiring a programmer
An RTF file built in Microsoft Word using the BI Publisher Template Builder add-in
A PNG image exported from OTBI
A Financial Reporting Studio grid definition
questions.explain: RTF templates built in Word with the Template Builder add-in let a report's visual design be built using familiar Word formatting.

questions.q: What is the typical first step in building a new BI Publisher template?
options: Uploading a finished PDF
Scheduling the report
Getting a sample XML data file from the data model to build the layout against
Deleting the existing data model
questions.explain: The workflow starts by obtaining sample XML, which the template author then maps fields and loops against while designing the layout in Word.

questions.q: What does a "field" represent in a BI Publisher RTF template?
options: A loop that repeats a table row
A single placeholder tied to one specific XML element from the data model's output
A parameter the user supplies before running the report
An entire data set
questions.explain: A field is a single placeholder — for example, mapping "Supplier Name" in the layout to the Supplier Name element in the XML.

questions.q: What does a "loop" do in a BI Publisher template, such as around a table row?
options: It deletes repeating rows from the output
It repeats a chunk of the layout once per row in a repeating data set, producing a multi-row listing at run time
It converts the template into a data model
It only works with header data sets, never detail data sets
questions.explain: A loop lets one table-row definition in the template produce many rows of actual output, one for each row in the underlying repeating data set.

questions.q: What is a common first mistake when building a template's loop around a table row?
options: Forgetting to add a title to the report
Wrapping the loop around the header fields as well as the detail fields, instead of only the repeating detail portion
Using too many parameters
Choosing PDF as an output format
questions.explain: Getting the loop boundaries wrong — including header content inside the repeating loop — is identified as the most common cause of malformed first-attempt output.
